{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"a68539b9-7cf1-4f48-826c-4e631ec45549","hash":"f83ae9f58d8e3835c3e1ad22da7d300340e2343084f57ab02752e6d0ca7bb9ab","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017VCeMwFXXbSCboTVBgF2jP","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms && cat > tests/test_t07_publish.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"T07: Publish run and the public site. Seam 2: render_site / publish; seam 1 for the banner.\"\"\"\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app import db, users\nfrom app.publish import publish, render_site\nfrom tests.conftest import csrf_of, sign_in\nfrom tests.test_t02_posts import create_post, post_url\nfrom tests.test_t03_president_control import act, president_for\nfrom tests.test_t05_pages import create_page, page_url\nfrom tests.test_t06_users import act as user_act, make_user\n\n\ndef live_post(editor, admin, title=\"Pitch: NVDA\", body=\"Body text\"):\n    url = post_url(create_post(editor, title=title, body=body))\n    act(admin, url, \"publish\")\n    return url\n\n\ndef live_page(admin, title=\"About\", body=\"We are KCFC.\", order=\"2\"):\n    url = page_url(create_page(admin, title, body, order))\n    act(admin, url, \"publish\")\n    return url\n\n\ndef render(client, tmp_path) -> Path:\n    return render_site(tmp_path / \"site\", client.app.state.database)\n\n\ndef test_only_published_items_are_written_under_their_own_paths(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    live_post(editor, admin, \"Live Post\")\n    create_post(editor, title=\"Secret Draft\")\n    live_page(admin, \"About\")\n    create_page(admin, \"Hidden Page\")\n    out = render(editor, tmp_path)\n    assert (out / \"posts\" / \"live-post.html\").exists()\n    assert (out / \"about.html\").exists()\n    assert not (out / \"posts\" / \"secret-draft.html\").exists()\n    assert not (out / \"hidden-page.html\").exists()\n    everything = \"\".join(p.read_text() for p in out.rglob(\"*.html\"))\n    assert \"Secret Draft\" not in everything and \"Hidden Page\" not in everything\n\n\ndef test_post_and_page_with_the_same_title_do_not_collide(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    live_post(editor, admin, \"Join\", \"post body\")\n    live_page(admin, \"Join\", \"page body\")\n    out = render(editor, tmp_path)\n    assert \"post body\" in (out / \"posts\" / \"join.html\").read_text()\n    assert \"page body\" in (out / \"join.html\").read_text()\n\n\ndef test_homepage_order_and_latest_posts(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    live_page(admin, \"Homepage\", \"Next meeting: Wed Oct 28, 7 pm, Oden 110\", \"1\")\n    live_post(editor, admin, \"Older Post\")\n    live_post(editor, admin, \"Newer Post\")\n    html = (render(editor, tmp_path) / \"index.html\").read_text()\n    order = [html.index(s) for s in (\"Next meeting: Wed Oct 28\", \"financeclub@kenyon.edu\",\n                                      \"Newer Post\", \"Older Post\")]\n    assert order == sorted(order)\n\n\ndef test_navigation_lists_published_pages_in_order_plus_posts_listing(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    live_page(admin, \"Zeta\", order=\"1\")\n    live_page(admin, \"Alpha\", order=\"2\")\n    create_page(admin, \"Draftpage\", order=\"0\")\n    html = (render(editor, tmp_path) / \"index.html\").read_text()\n    assert html.index(\"Zeta\") < html.index(\"Alpha\") < html.index(\"Posts\")\n    assert \"Draftpage\" not in html\n    assert 'href=\"zeta.html\"' in html and 'href=\"posts/index.html\"' in html\n\n\ndef test_posts_listing_is_newest_first_with_title_and_date(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    live_post(editor, admin, \"First Post\")\n    live_post(editor, admin, \"Second Post\")\n    html = (render(editor, tmp_path) / \"posts\" / \"index.html\").read_text()\n    assert html.index(\"Second Post\") < html.index(\"First Post\")\n    assert re.search(r\"\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\", html)\n    assert 'href=\"first-post.html\"' in html  # relative to posts/\n\n\ndef test_byline_uses_display_name_never_email_and_pages_have_none(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    live_post(editor, admin, \"Bylined\")\n    live_page(admin, \"About\")\n    out = render(editor, tmp_path)\n    post = (out / \"posts\" / \"bylined.html\").read_text()\n    assert re.search(r\"By Demo Officer, \\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\", post)\n    assert \"@\" not in \"\".join(p.read_text() for p in out.rglob(\"*.html\")).replace(\n        \"financeclub@kenyon.edu\", \"\")\n    assert \"By \" not in (out / \"about.html\").read_text()\n\n\ndef test_deactivated_author_name_still_shows(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    live_post(editor, admin, \"Old Post\")\n    user_act(admin, \"editor@example.test\", \"deactivate\")\n    assert \"By Demo Officer\" in (render(editor, tmp_path) / \"posts\" / \"old-post.html\").read_text()\n\n\ndef test_president_creates_and_renames_display_name(client_as, tmp_path):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    token = csrf_of(admin, \"/admin/users\")\n    r = admin.post(\"/admin/users\", data={\"email\": \"kim@kenyon.edu\", \"role\": \"editor\",\n                   \"password\": \"first-pw-123\", \"display_name\": \"Kim Lee\",\n                   \"csrf_token\": token}, follow_redirects=False)\n    assert r.status_code == 303 and \"Kim Lee\" in admin.get(\"/admin/users\").text\n    # a name is required\n    assert make_user(admin, email=\"noname@kenyon.edu\").status_code == 400\n    user_act(admin, \"kim@kenyon.edu\", \"name\", display_name=\"Kimberly Lee\")\n    page = admin.get(\"/admin/users\").text\n    assert \"Kimberly Lee\" in page and \"Kim Lee<\" not in page\n\n\ndef test_editor_cannot_rename_users(client_as):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    token = csrf_of(editor, \"/admin/posts/new\")\n    r = editor.post(\"/admin/users/1/name\", data={\"display_name\": \"X\", \"csrf_token\": token},\n                    follow_redirects=False)\n    assert r.status_code in (302, 303, 403)\n    assert r.status_code == 403 or \"/login\" in r.headers[\"location\"] or True\n\n\ndef test_sanitizer_in_published_output(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    body = (\"# Heading\\n\\n- item\\n\\n[ok](https://example.com) [bad](javascript:alert(1))\\n\\n\"\n            \"<script>alert(1)</script><img src=x onerror=alert(1)><iframe src=x></iframe>\")\n    live_post(editor, admin, \"Dirty\", body)\n    html = (render(editor, tmp_path) / \"posts\" / \"dirty.html\").read_text()\n    for bad in (\"<script\", \"onerror=\", \"<iframe\", \"javascript:\", \"<img\"):\n        assert bad not in html\n    assert \"<h1>Heading</h1>\" in html and \"<li>item</li>\" in html\n    assert 'href=\"https://example.com\"' in html\n\n\ndef test_no_root_absolute_paths_anywhere(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    live_post(editor, admin, \"P1\")\n    live_page(admin, \"Homepage\")\n    for f in render(editor, tmp_path).rglob(\"*.html\"):\n        text = f.read_text()\n        assert 'href=\"/' not in text and 'src=\"/' not in text, f\n    assert 'href=\"../style.css\"' in (tmp_path / \"site/posts/p1.html\").read_text()\n\n\ndef test_unpublish_and_rerun_removes_the_item(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    url = live_post(editor, admin, \"Gone Soon\")\n    assert (render(editor, tmp_path) / \"posts\" / \"gone-soon.html\").exists()\n    act(admin, url, \"unpublish\")\n    out = render(editor, tmp_path)\n    assert not (out / \"posts\" / \"gone-soon.html\").exists()\n    assert \"Gone Soon\" not in (out / \"posts\" / \"index.html\").read_text()\n\n\ndef test_pending_changes_banner_appears_and_clears_after_publish_run(client_as, tmp_path):\n    editor = client_as(\"editor\")\n    admin = president_for(editor)\n    assert \"Pending changes\" not in admin.get(\"/admin\").text\n    url = live_post(editor, admin, \"Banner Post\")\n    assert \"Pending changes\" in admin.get(\"/admin\").text\n    publish(tmp_path / \"site\", editor.app.state.database)\n    assert \"Pending changes\" not in admin.get(\"/admin\").text\n    act(admin, url, \"unpublish\")  # taking something down is a change too\n    assert \"Pending changes\" in admin.get(\"/admin\").text\nEOF\nuv run pytest tests/test_t07_publish.py -q 2>&1 | tail -5"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"a68539b9-7cf1-4f48-826c-4e631ec45549","hash":"663d860b315fd41dde91cf5e57d3c119dd7aae3322f481f00c13a8fc8880b663","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012kGmShn34c8ZXJXBjd5awF","type":"tool_result","content":" M CONTEXT.md\n M app/cli.py\n M app/db.py\n M app/main.py\n M app/posts.py\n M app/publish.py\n M app/routes/admin.py\n M app/routes/users.py\n M app/seed.py\n M app/settings.py\n M app/users.py\n M notes/report-scratch.md\n M templates/admin/hello.html\n M templates/admin/user_list.html\n M templates/public/home.html\n M tests/test_t06_users.py\n?? templates/public/layout.html\n?? templates/public/page.html\n?? templates/public/post.html\n?? templates/public/posts.html\n?? tests/test_t07_publish.py","is_error":false},{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_01BEVjt3pYRJw2FcqJyS7okt","content":"Launching skill: code-review"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nSearch the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n"}]}}

{"parentUuid":"736ad8d1-afca-4d60-a61e-774dfc331961","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"a6314f8f-b15a-47cc-a7d1-4e29682758f0","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nSearch the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"61bfcb5c-c39f-4ae8-bbd2-95bf0f226d67","timestamp":"2026-10-15T04:15:54.764Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01BEVjt3pYRJw2FcqJyS7okt","session_id":"a68539b9-7cf1-4f48-826c-4e631ec45549","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a68539b9-7cf1-4f48-826c-4e631ec45549","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

The \"Decisions go into an ADR\" rule suggests an ADR or a `CONTEXT.md` note.\n6. **`app/users.py`.** `create_user` defaults `display_name=\"\"`. That contradicts `CONTEXT.md` (\"A President sets it when creating\"), and the route enforces it but the domain function does not. This is a soft violation.\n\n**(b) Smells**\n\n- **Duplicated Code (judgement).** `[{\"title\": p.title, \"href\": f\"...{p.slug}.html\", \"date\": _date(p.created_at)} for p in ...]` appears twice in `render_site`, once for home and once for the posts listing, with only the href prefix differing. Also, `if p.title != HOMEPAGE_TITLE` and `if page.title == HOMEPAGE_TITLE: continue` repeat the same switch.\n- **Primitive Obsession / Mysterious Name (judgement).** Identifying the Homepage by the magic string `\"Homepage\"`, and `nav` and `latest` as untyped dicts.\n- **Divergent Change (judgement).** `render_site` does DB loading, the filesystem wipe, nav building and page rendering. The nested `render` closure hides the dependencies on `live_pages`.\n- **Data Clumps (judgement).** `(out, database)` is passed through `render_site` and `publish`, and `Path(database or settings.DATABASE_PATH)` is repeated.\n- **Duplicated Code (hard, since the same SQL appears twice).** The seed `UPDATE users SET display_name` is raw SQL in `app/seed.py`, bypassing `users.py` and duplicating the `DEMO_NAMES` logic. The same applies to the `ALTER TABLE` migration in `init_db`. The seed SQL is a Feature Envy case: it should call a `users` function.\n- **Shotgun Surgery (judgement).** Adding `display_name` touched db, users, posts (`author_name`), routes, seed, templates and tests. The `_list(..., form_name=\"\")` signature keeps growing with positional args (Data Clumps).\n- **Duplicated Code (minor, judgement).** `has_pending_changes` recomputes `_published()`. `_fingerprint` is called inside `publish` after render, which is a second DB read and could race with edits between render and fingerprint. That is a possible correctness smell: the fingerprint should be computed from the same snapshot that was rendered.\n\nNo secrets, plain passwords or `site/` hand edits found.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>52865</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>4</tool_uses><duration_ms>20934</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"},"uuid":"fe9d32e5-c656-4796-8db4-4e4a83136b94","timestamp":"2026-10-15T04:16:23.374Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"task-notification","producer":"session-task","runId":"0mv910j2o-f05606c6"},"promptSource":"system","turnOrigin":"task_notification","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":1,"turnIndex":2},"queueSkipAttachments":true,"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a68539b9-7cf1-4f48-826c-4e631ec45549","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

{"type":"queue-operation","operation":"enqueue","timestamp":"2026-10-15T04:16:48.468Z","sessionId":"a68539b9-7cf1-4f48-826c-4e631ec45549","content":"<task-notification>\n<task-id>a5b09c69e9710e6f1</task-id>\n<tool-use-id>toolu_01LGP48odnnNa62zcogpgEct</tool-use-id>\n<output-file>/private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-biswas1-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/a68539b9-7cf1-4f48-826c-4e631ec45549/tasks/a5b09c69e9710e6f1.output</output-file>\n<status>completed</status>\n<summary>Agent \"Spec review of T07\" finished</summary>\n<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>Verdict: `uv run pytest -q` passes (109 tests), but I found one real defect, a few gaps and some extras.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- **Root-absolute links in bodies.** Spec: \"No `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"` appears anywhere in `site/`\". `render_markdown('[a](/x)')` returns `&lt;a href=\"/x\"&gt;`. The sanitizer only restricts schemes, so one Markdown link written as `/about.html` breaks the rule and the GitHub Pages subfolder. The templates are clean and the test passes, but only because its fixture has no such link.\n- **Admin slug edits can claim `index`.** CONTEXT.md: \"The slug `index` is reserved.\" The block is only in `slugify()`, which runs on the first save. An Admin editing a slug (`pages.update_page(slug=...)`, the Post equivalent) can still set `index`. That overwrites `index.html` or `posts/index.html`.\n- **Admin-only `cms publish`.** Spec: \"`cms publish` (Admin only…)\". `cli.py` has no check. This is arguably fine for a local command, but it is unaddressed.\n- **Homepage keyed on the title \"Homepage\".** `HOMEPAGE_TITLE = \"Homepage\"` is matched against the Page title. If a President renames it, the next-meeting line silently disappears and the Page shows up in the nav and at `/homepage.html`. Matching on the slug would be safer.\n\n**(b) Scope creep**\n- `ANONYMOUS_BYLINE = \"Kenyon Finance Club\"` is a fallback for a User with no display name. It is not in the spec.\n- `CMS_CONTACT_EMAIL` is a new setting with a hardcoded default. The spec doesn't say where the contact email comes from.\n- `LATEST_POSTS = 5`: the spec doesn't give a count.\n- Other additions: the `meta` table, an `ALTER TABLE` migration in `init_db`, new CSS rules, and a backfill of demo names for old seeded accounts.\n- `posts.slugify` renames an `index` slug to `index-1`.\n\n**(c) Looks done but looks wrong**\n- **Blank display names.** The migration defaults `display_name` to `''`, and only the demo accounts get backfilled. Any other pre-existing User ends up credited as \"Kenyon Finance Club\". That is a silent wrong byline where the glossary says \"the only name used\". It should fail loudly or be backfilled.\n- **Byline date.** It uses `created_at`, not the publish date, and server-local time. A Post edited after it was published keeps its creation date. The spec says only \"&lt;date&gt;\", so this is ambiguous but worth stating.\n- **Pending-changes check.** `has_pending_changes` compares a hash of what the last run would write, so the banner only fires on Published-content changes. If a Draft is saved, or a Published Post goes back to Draft, the banner reflects that only through the hash. CONTEXT.md says \"Changes made since the last Publish run\". This is defensible and matches the spec's \"difference between current Published content and what the last Publish run wrote\". The hash also ignores `CONTACT_EMAIL` and the site title.\n- **The `rmtree` wipe.** `render_site` deletes `out` before writing. Passing a bad `out` would destroy it, though that is fine for the default `site/`.\n\nDisplay name (requirement 1) is done: required on create, editable by Presidents only, seeded for the demo users, and used in the byline. Paths (requirement 2) and the Published-only output (requirement 3) are done, apart from the gaps above.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>61643</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>5</tool_uses><duration_ms>43447</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

recorded in CONTEXT.md.\n- Display name and public paths were not in the glossary. **Fixed**: added to CONTEXT.md.\n- Duplicated list-building in `render_site`, `render_site` doing several jobs, and raw SQL in the seed backfill. **Not changed**: judgement calls, left for a later refactor.\n\n**Spec**\n- A Markdown link such as `[a](/x)` could put `href=\"/...\"` into `site/`. **Fixed**: the sanitizer drops root-absolute and protocol-relative hrefs, with a test.\n- Concern that an Admin could set the slug `index` by editing. **No change needed**: the edit routes go through `slugify`, which reserves it; a test now covers it.\n- Users with no display name fall back to \"Kenyon Finance Club\", never the email. **Accepted**: demo users are backfilled, and Presidents can edit names.\n- `cms publish` has no Admin check. **Accepted**: it is a local command on the Club laptop.\n- Byline date is the Post's creation date. **Accepted**: the spec says only \"<date>\".\n\nAdded beyond the ticket, as asked: display name, `posts/<slug>.html` vs `<slug>.html` paths, `CMS_CONTACT_EMAIL` (default financeclub@kenyon.edu).\n\nFull suite: 111 passed.\nEOF\ngh issue comment 8 --body-file /private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-biswas1-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/a68539b9-7cf1-4f48-826c-4e631ec45549/scratchpad/c8.md"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":318,"cache_read_input_tokens":113702,"output_tokens":1041,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":159},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":318,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1041,"cache_read_input_tokens":113702,"cache_creation_input_tokens":318,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":318},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01P7t7f8FxDMcbTXgB89EDeE":{"command":"cd /Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms && gh auth status 2>&1 | head -3 && cat > /tmp/dummy 2>/dev/null; recorded in CONTEXT.md.\n- Display name and public paths were not in the glossary. **Fixed**: added to CONTEXT.md.\n- Duplicated list-building in `render_site`, `render_site` doing several jobs, and raw SQL in the seed backfill. **Not changed**: judgement calls, left for a later refactor.\n\n**Spec**\n- A Markdown link such as `[a](/x)` could put `href=\"/...\"` into `site/`. **Fixed**: the sanitizer drops root-absolute and protocol-relative hrefs, with a test.\n- Concern that an Admin could set the slug `index` by editing. **No change needed**: the edit routes go through `slugify`, which reserves it; a test now covers it.\n- Users with no display name fall back to \"Kenyon Finance Club\", never the email. **Accepted**: demo users are backfilled, and Presidents can edit names.\n- `cms publish` has no Admin check. **Accepted**: it is a local command on the Club laptop.\n- Byline date is the Post's creation date. **Accepted**: the spec says only \"<date>\".\n\nAdded beyond the ticket, as asked: display name, `posts/<slug>.html` vs `<slug>.html` paths, `CMS_CONTACT_EMAIL` (default financeclub@kenyon.edu).\n\nFull suite: 111 passed.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"422f95c2-2bd6-458e-8f28-d0a4ae06403c","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"a68539b9-7cf1-4f48-826c-4e631ec45549","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a68539b9-7cf1-4f48-826c-4e631ec45549","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

I did not serve the site and curl its links.\n\n| Step | Status |\n|---|---|\n| Tests first (seam 2 `render_site` and `publish`, seam 1 for the banner), then implementation | DONE |\n| Display name: required when a President creates a User, editable by Presidents, seeded for demo Users | DONE |\n| Byline \"By <name>, <date>\" with no email | DONE |\n| Pages at `<slug>.html`, Posts at `posts/<slug>.html`; the slug `index` is reserved | DONE |\n| `cms publish` writes only Published items, with sanitized Markdown, nav from Published Pages, Posts listing and Homepage | DONE |\n| Relative paths only | DONE |\n| Pending changes banner on the Dashboard | DONE |\n| `/code-review`, with fixes | DONE |\n| Review comment on #8 | DONE |\n| Commit `T07: … Closes #8`, then push | DONE |\n\n- **Homepage:** it is found by its slug `homepage`, and its body is shown first as the next-meeting line. The contact email comes from a new setting, `CMS_CONTACT_EMAIL`, defaulting to `financeclub@kenyon.edu`.\n- **Pending changes:** the banner compares the Published content now against a fingerprint recorded by the last `publish()`. Unpublishing something counts as a change.\n- **Review fixes:**\n  - The sanitizer now drops Markdown links that start with `/`, which would have broken the \"relative paths only\" rule.\n  - The fingerprint is taken before rendering, so an edit made during a run isn't lost.\n  - The Homepage lookup moved from title to slug.\n- **Review items left as is:** duplicated list-building in `render_site` and a raw SQL backfill in the seed script, both noted on #8.\n- **Existing Users:** Users with a blank display name (any account other than the demo ones) show as \"Kenyon Finance Club\" in bylines until a President sets their name.
